prompt: Some people believe that newspapers and websites should be free to publish stories about the private lives of famous people. Others think that famous people have the same right to privacy as anyone else. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
essay:
The private lives of famous people have always sold newspapers, and online publishing has only increased the appetite for such stories. While I accept that some public figures forfeit part of their privacy, I believe that for most famous people, most of the time, the right to a private life should be protected.

Those who defend intrusive reporting usually make two arguments. The first is that fame is a bargain: actors, athletes and musicians benefit enormously from public attention, and many actively invite it by sharing details of their relationships and homes. It seems inconsistent for them to welcome coverage when it promotes a film and object to it when it reveals a divorce. The second, and stronger, argument concerns people with power. When a politician who campaigns on family values is found to be deceiving his own family, or a minister has undisclosed business interests, the press is exposing hypocrisy or corruption that voters are entitled to know about.

Those who favour stronger protection point out that most celebrity stories involve no such public interest. Photographs of an actor's children on the way to school or reports of a singer's medical treatment tell readers nothing that matters to them; they simply satisfy curiosity. The cost to the person concerned can be severe, since constant pursuit by photographers makes an ordinary life almost impossible, and the harm falls also on relatives who never sought fame at all.

In my view, the second position is more convincing, although the first contains an important exception. Politicians and others who exercise power over the public should expect scrutiny of any private conduct that relates to that power. Entertainers, however, have sold their performances rather than their lives, and publishing their private information purely because readers are curious should not be permitted.
title: Reporting on the private lives of the famous
